Enum Class LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction>
io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Comparable<LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction>, Constable
Enclosing interface:
LogAlerts
public static enum LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction extends Enum<LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction>
What LogLifecycle.start(LogConfig) does if, at that moment, at least one alert has been recorded and still zero LogAlerts.Listeners are registered - the situation Logback's StatusManager calls an unobserved status: nothing is watching, so whatever went wrong during property loading or a RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator would otherwise only ever have reached the individual, easy to miss stderr lines each LogAlerts.error(LogEvent) call already produces.

Deliberately keyed as "logging.alerts.unobservedErrorsAction" (an enum, not a boolean) since "fail" without "dump" first would throw away the only diagnostic evidence of why it failed.

  • Enum Constant Details

    • NONE

      public static final LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction NONE
      Do nothing beyond what LogAlerts.error(LogEvent) already does per event.

    • DUMP

      public static final LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction DUMP
      Default. Report the whole backlog to MetaLog as one clearly labeled block, the same way Logback auto-installs a console listener and prints its accumulated status if nothing else is watching by the end of configuration - RainbowGum still starts.

    • FAIL

      public static final LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction FAIL
      Same reporting as DUMP, but then throws, so LogConfig.Builder.build() (and therefore whatever is building a RainbowGum from it) never completes. Goes further than Logback ever does - an explicit, opt-in choice of integrity over resilience for deployments where a silently-broken bootstrap is worse than refusing to start.
